sections.content:
135,090 people

were counted on the census as "road transport drivers (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.
People who do this type of work drive other transport vehicles in roles not elsewhere classified.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "road transport drivers (other)" there were more men than women (94.1% compared with 5.9%).

This means "road transport drivers (other)" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "transport and mobile machine drivers and operatives".

Men made up 94.1% and women made up 5.9% of "road transport drivers (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "road transport drivers (other)" included:

  • construction and building trades supervisors
  • ship and hovercraft officers
  • telecoms and related network installers and repairers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "road transport drivers (other)" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "road transport drivers (other)", 14.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "road transport drivers (other)" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "road transport drivers (other)" included:

  • personal assistants and other secretaries
  • officers of non-governmental organisations
  • painters and decorators

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "road transport drivers (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "road transport drivers (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "road transport drivers (other)", 9.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (72.3% compared with 27.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (75.5%) than self-employed (24.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
